title: Doubting what you already know: uncertainty regarding state transitions and OCD symptoms
author: Isaac Fradkin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.97nh9me

steps.title: Present initial deterministic instructions
steps.instruction: Read to the participant, with the experimenter present, that three cues will appear, only one cue predicts the circle location, the other two are random, and that this predictive cue will change (shift) at some point.

steps.title: Conduct deterministic training with experimenter
steps.instruction: Run a training session while the experimenter stays in the room.

substeps.instruction: After a few trials, verify that the participant is responding according to the relevant cue and ask which cue is relevant.
If the participant answers incorrectly, tell them to check the cues again and continue training.
After the shift, ask the participant whether they noticed that a shift occurred.
If the participant failed to learn the first or second cue, re‑explain the task and repeat the training from the start.
When training is complete, the experimenter leaves the room.

steps.title: Run deterministic test block
steps.instruction: Administer the main deterministic phase consisting of 88 trials.

substeps.instruction: Counterbalance shift timing: for each participant the shift occurs after either 40 or 48 trials.
‑ Show a fixation cross for 1000 ms.
‑ Display the three cues and wait for a response (maximum 900 ms).
‑ Present the target circle for a duration uniformly drawn between 1000 ms and 1200 ms.
Note that the target appears regardless of whether the participant responded or how they responded.

steps.title: Present probabilistic instructions
steps.instruction: With the experimenter present, read to the participant that the relevant cue will now predict the circle location on most trials (75 %) rather than all, and confirm understanding.

steps.title: Run probabilistic block
steps.instruction: Run the probabilistic phase without additional training, using the same trial structure as before but with a 75 % cue‑predictive probability.

substeps.instruction: Shift timing is opposite to the deterministic block: if the deterministic shift occurred after 40 trials, the probabilistic shift occurs after 48 trials; if it occurred after 48 trials, the probabilistic shift occurs after 40 trials.
For each trial, repeat the fixation (1000 ms), cue (up to 900 ms), and target (1000‑1200 ms) sequence.
